June 11th.

Sent to the senate Monday in answer to a resolution of February last calling for information relative to reciprocity negotiations with Canada, the president sounds the death knell of the project and plants a mile post in American history by deliberately recommending that we proceed to retaliate upon the Canadas for its persistent denial of the rights of American citizens intended by the treaty of Washington.

McKenzie and Hon. Geo. Foster. Hon. M. W. Foster also appeared on behalf of the government of the United States at the request of the secretary of state. The president says:

"The result of the conferences, as to the feasibility of arranging a reciprocity treaty with the Dominion of Canada, is clearly stated in the letter of Mr. Blaine, and was anticipated, I think, by him and every thoughtful American who had considered the subject, a reciprocity treaty limited to the exchange of natural products would have been such only in form. It is not for the government to argue against this announcement of Canadian officials. It must be accepted, however, I think, as the statement of a condition which places an insuperate barrier in the way of attainment of that large and beneficial intercourse and reciprocal trade which might otherwise be developed between the United States and the Dominion."

that they desire to reward Wotring
for his excellent work as chairman
during the last election. Then,
again, they have a grievance against
Fortney for insubordination during
the last campaign in refusing to go
forth and take the stump and
preach the gospel of Republicanism
from every empty school house that
would give him an audience, and
Neil would rather suffer martyrdom
than be left in the wilderness with
no one within the sound of his
voice and have to walk home by
himself" and the political worker
could not restrain his laughter when
he recollected the fate of the other
stump speakers who were greeted
with open doors and empty seats in
their wild harangue to be granted
further lease in toying with the
Government teat, while the politi-
cal workers were sent out to hustle
in the faithful on election day.
Yes, the refusal of Fortney to
take the stump and sign certain
papers, which I am not at liberty to
disclose, was reported to the State
Bosses, and they instructed the
Controllers to quietly lay him on
the shelf and for Wotring to be
given Neil's shoes, even if Dave had
to split them and rip them at the
heel to get them on, and as true
Knights of the Spells, we have to
obey orders. As former supporter
of the man who is to be dethroned,
when he was our standard bearer,
thought it no more than right
that he be given an inkling of what
was going on in the inner circle, so
he will be prepared to move when we
turn the office over to David Mel-
anthon Wotring, and the politi-
cal worker drifted over to the Jour-
nal to consult on further nomina-
tions.


This will be sad news to the
numerous friends of the popular
and jovial Prosecuting Attorney,
to learn that he is to be turned
down simply because he refused to
neglect his official duty and axe
the stump for political party. Is
that what we elect Prosecuting At-
torney, to go around making politi-
cal and partisan speeches? And to
think that he has been ordered to
be sacrificed by politicians who live
outside of Preston. We imagine
the rank and file of the party will
have something to say in regard to
this before Neil J. Fortney is turned
down by the dictates of outside in-
terlopers.

ment house.

Congregational church on the following
successive Sunday evenings. The topics

third lecture to young men. Evening
service will begin at 7.30 o'clock. Love
feast at 9.30 o'clock in the morning.
